title_en: Chen Jianming — Refusal to Execute a Court Judgment Case
keywords_en: Criminal; Crime of Refusing to Execute Judgments or Rulings; First Instance; Basic People's Court; Zhejiang Province; Natural Person; Criminal Law; Civil Procedure Law; Whether Refusing to Execute a Mediation Agreement Constitutes a Crime; Having Ability to Perform but Refusing to Execute; Partial Support; Debt Dispute; Mediation Agreement; Refusal to Execute; Fleeing the Country
full_text_en:
**Chen Jianming — refusal to comply with a legally effective judgment of a people's court**

**Defendant:** Chen Jianming, male, 29 years old, a native of Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province, unemployed. Arrested on August 9, 1993.

The case of Chen Jianming for refusal to comply with a legally effective judgment of a people's court was accepted for trial by the Gongshu District People's Court of Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province in accordance with law. The court, after a public hearing, found the following facts:

The defendant, Chen Jianming, and Zhao Suying had a debt dispute. In October 1989, under the auspices of the Gongshu District People's Court of Hangzhou, both parties voluntarily reached a mediation agreement: from October 1989 to November 1992, Chen Jianming would pay Zhao Suying principal and interest in monthly installments totaling RMB 60,400. After the mediation agreement became legally effective, Chen Jianming paid only RMB 2,000 in the first two months and thereafter failed to make further payments. Consequently, in January 1990, Zhao Suying applied to the Gongshu District People's Court for compulsory execution. The court took compulsory measures such as transferring funds from the bank account of a braised delicacy shop operated by Chen Jianming and sealing the shop premises, forcing him to repay RMB 12,630 in installments. During the subsequent enforcement process, Chen Jianming continued to operate the braised delicacy shop and had the ability to repay the debt, but he ignored repeated admonitions and notices from the court and failed to pay the overdue amounts on time. In April 1991, the Gongshu District People's Court summoned Chen Jianming to appear in court. Chen Jianming falsely stated that he would pay part of the outstanding amount within a few days. However, three days later, Chen Jianming actually closed the shop and fled with his wife, children, and mother, taking their savings with them. During this period, Chen Jianming opened roast poultry shops in Sanming City, Fujian Province, and Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province. It was not until July 30, 1993, that Chen Jianming was arrested in accordance with law when he secretly returned to Hangzhou. After Chen Jianming's arrest, Zhao Suying and Chen Jianming reached an enforcement settlement agreement, whereby Chen Jianming would repay RMB 30,000 in a lump sum, and Zhao Suying voluntarily waived the remaining claims. With the assistance of his family members, Chen Jianming delivered RMB 20,000 and USD 1,000 to Zhao Suying.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including the Civil Mediation Document No. (1989) Hang Gong Fa Min Zi 258, which has already become legally effective; Zhao Suying's application for enforcement; the enforcement notice of the Gongshu District People's Court; records of the enforcement personnel's multiple attempts to educate the defendant; and the testimony of witnesses Wang Huiying, Li Xianrun, and Deng Yanjun. The defendant, Chen Jianming, also confessed to the facts of his refusal to comply, and the evidence is sufficient to establish the facts.

The Gongshu District People's Court of Hangzhou held that: The debt dispute between the defendant, Chen Jianming, and Zhao Suying was voluntarily settled by both parties through a mediation agreement under the auspices of the people's court. This mediation agreement is not only a record of the negotiation results between the parties but also a legal document through which the people's court recognizes and approves the agreement between the parties. After being signed and received by both parties, it has the same legal effect as a legally effective judgment or ruling. The defendant, Chen Jianming, disregarded national law; despite having the ability to perform, he refused to comply with the legally effective mediation agreement, using deceptive and evasive methods to openly refuse enforcement. His conduct was of a serious nature. Pursuant to Article 102, Paragraph 1, Item (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 123, Item (3) of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, he should be punished in accordance with the crime of refusal to comply with a judgment of a people's court as provided in Article 157 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. Considering that after being brought to justice, the defendant, Chen Jianming, showed a relatively good attitude in admitting his guilt and urged his family to pay RMB 20,000 and USD 1,000, a lighter punishment may be imposed, and as the application of probation would not cause further harm to society, a suspended sentence may be pronounced in accordance with Article 67, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 126 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China — which provides that "where, according to Article 102, Paragraph 1, Item (6) of the Civil Procedure Law, the criminal liability of a person concerned should be pursued, the criminal trial division of the people's court shall directly accept and hear the case and render a judgment" — the Gongshu District People's Court of Hangzhou rendered the following judgment on September 17, 1993:

The defendant, Chen Jianming, is guilty of the crime of refusal to comply with a judgment of a people's court and is sentenced to six months' imprisonment, suspended for one year.

After the judgment was pronounced, the defendant, Chen Jianming, stated that he accepted his guilt and submitted to the judgment, and did not file an appeal.
